title: pkix-ct: 49 of 91 survivors are Vec::with_capacity arithmetic, equivalent by construction
description:
## What

The first pkix-ct sweep (2026-11-27) reported 91 missed in 452 mutants --
the largest survivor count of the campaign. 49 of them are on four lines:

    verify.rs:1237  let cap = 1 + 1 + 8 + 2 + 3 + cert_len + 2 + sct.extensions.len();
    verify.rs:1265  let cap = 1 + 1 + 8 + 2 + 32 + 3 + tbs_len + 2 + sct.extensions.len();
    verify.rs:1331  let cap = 1 + 1 + 8 + 2 + 3 + cert_len + 2 + sct.extensions.len();
    verify.rs:1372  let cap = 1 + 1 + 8 + 2 + 32 + 3 + tbs_len + 2 + sct.extensions.len();

Each feeds `Vec::with_capacity(cap)` and nothing else. Every `+ -> *` and
`+ -> -` mutant on them changes how much the vector pre-allocates and not
one byte of what it contains, so no test can distinguish them and none
should try. `Vec` grows on demand; a wrong hint costs a realloc.

## Why it is worth a bead rather than a fix

49 survivors is most of the crate's reported total, and a reader seeing
91 would reasonably conclude pkix-ct is the least-tested crate in the
workspace. It is not: the figure is dominated by one idiom repeated four
times. The real set is 42, and the clusters are:

    6   `if X.len() > MAX_ASN1_CERT_LEN` -- the RFC 6962 §3.2
        `opaque ASN.1Cert<1..2^24-1>` boundary, at four builders plus
        verify_embedded_scts_with_report and one more. Pinning it needs a
        16 MiB buffer, which a test can allocate rather than commit.
    4   `(len >> 16) & 0xFF` -> `<<` -- the top octet of the 3-byte
        length prefix. `<< 16` makes the low 8 bits zero, so every
        certificate over 64 KiB gets a wrong prefix. A known-answer wire
        test over a >64 KiB input kills all four.
    3   verify.rs:1060, `64 - (tree_size - 1).leading_zeros()` -- the
        Merkle proof depth.
    17  log_list.rs
    8   raw_der.rs
    1   lib.rs, 1 delivery.rs

## How to read a future sweep

Expect ~49 capacity-hint survivors in this crate and do not count them.
A comment at each `cap` line now says so. If the count moves, a `cap`
expression started feeding something other than `with_capacity`, which
would be worth looking at.

## Found by

The pkix-ct sweep, 2026-11-27. Recorded under PKIX-9bzr.
notes:
## Progress, 2026-11-27 (late)

91 -> 70 -> now expected ~55. Commits 4b529416, 7fb723de, 1d9d4dd7.

Closed: the four u24 shifts, read_tlv's six length edges, the RFC 3339
parser's separators / fractional seconds / epoch boundary / leap
exceptions, Error's Display, CtLogList::is_empty, and the x509 ASN.1Cert
ceiling.

## A mistake of mine worth keeping

My first leap-year test asserted 1900-02-29 is refused. It is -- but 1900
is before the epoch, so `secs < 0` refuses it whatever the leap rule
decides. The assertion passed with the rule inverted and both `% 100`
mutants stayed alive under a test that read as though it covered them.
2100 is the century non-leap year that is not masked.

Same shape as the overdetermined guards in AGENTS.md, except the
subsuming check was inside the code under test rather than beside it. A
negative assertion is only evidence if the input reaches the rule it
names. Worth checking for any test whose expected outcome is an error:
ask which check produces it.

## Accounted for, not open

49  Vec::with_capacity hint arithmetic on four `let cap = ...` lines.
3   verify.rs:1070, the audit-path length pre-check -- the loop below
    enforces `64 - leading_zeros(N - 1)` exactly, so the two bounds are
    the same expression written twice. See AGENTS.md, "sometimes
    subsumed means subsumed".
2   raw_der `|` against `^`, operands cannot overlap.
1   raw_der `after_first.len() < count` as `<=`.
2   log_list days_from_civil's negative-era branch, unreachable because
    pre-1970 is refused downstream.

All now carry a comment at the code saying so.

## Still open (~5)

5   The ASN.1Cert ceiling on the three paths that parse the certificate
    rather than taking it as bytes: build_merkle_tree_leaf_precert_entry,
    build_signed_input_precert_entry, build_signed_input_x509_entry,
    verify_embedded_scts_with_report and tbs_without_sct_list. Each needs
    a genuine certificate over 16 MiB, which is too large to commit --
    a test would have to construct one at runtime. Low value: the
    boundary is already pinned on the x509 MerkleTreeLeaf path, and these
    are the same constant compared the same way.
1   delivery.rs:131, the SCT-list OID in top-level responseExtensions.
    The existing fixture carries its SCTs in singleExtensions, so the
    fallback branch is entirely untested -- not just its comparison.
    RFC 6962 §3.3 allows either placement and some responders use the
    top level, so this is a real delivery path with no coverage. Needs a
    synthetic OCSP response; the function verifies no signature, so a
    generator can build one freely.
